item.title: emacs: patch CVE-2026-108976
item.description:
Incomplete fix for Emacs CVE-2026-79992

Wonyoung Jung of 78ResearchLab, using their PatchHawk tool, discovered that the fix for CVE-2026-79992 was incomplete.

The tramp-user-regexp failed to check for some additional problematic characters in user names, meaning that exploitation was still possible.

The attached patch by TRAMP maintainer Michael Albinus addresses the problem. It will be included in Emacs 31.2 though that won't be released soon.

Message and patch taken from: https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/11/1

Ref: #573231

item.title: openjpeg: fetch patch for CVE-2026-6192
item.description:
See https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6192 for details.

Tl;dr: unfixed vulnerability in openjpeg since earlier this year. Upstream is mostly unmaintained (https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/06bbae8b5d5e57f8c28fe862b80a9464b320e314). The CVE body suggests picking the patch commit, so this is what i did here. Also switched to finalAttrs (overriding doCheck = false would break without that fixpoint), and added a CPE identifier.

item.title: [Backport release-26.05] jellyfin-web: backport item details XSS fix
item.description:
My understanding of the attack:

This bug allows an attacker to update e.g. tmdb metadata on a popular item with an embedded xss script call, then wait for it to propagate through jellyfin servers into user browsers when they open the item details page, potentially stealing their session cookies. (If the user is admin, it gives even more power.)
